title: What Does Local Inference Add After Deterministic Tools? A Reproducible Agricultural Routing Case Study
affiliation_user_provided: Russian State Agrarian University - Moscow Timiryazev Agricultural Academy, Moscow, Russia
abstract: Local–cloud language-model cascades can reduce cloud use, but apparent gains may come primarily from deterministic tools. We examine this distinction in a reproducible agricultural question-answering case study on a 16-GB consumer GPU. A frozen controlled evaluation contains 150 cases, balanced between Russian and English, spanning six task categories and 25 documented source or scenario groups. Five policies produce 750 separately executed decisions. Tools plus cloud achieves 139/150 correct decisions; adding a local stage yields 133/150 while reducing cloud calls from 100 to 20. The paired quality difference is −4.00 percentage points, with a group-bootstrap 95% interval of [−17.65, +5.83]; the prespecified −5-point non-inferiority criterion is not met. Hybrid mean latency falls from 2.682 to 0.844 seconds. Compound answers expose a verifier failure: literal context support admits incorrect rule branches. We report token accounting, resource limits, offline behavior and procedural deviations. These results demonstrate a measured cost–quality tradeoff on controlled cases, not validated agronomic deployment. Human gold review and a more external source-disjoint evaluation remain necessary.
article_type: original empirical case study; negative/noninferiority result, not survey or novel-router claim
